   138	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   139	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   140	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   141	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   142	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   143	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   144	
   145	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   147	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   151	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   152	      intro j hj
   153	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   154	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   155	
   156	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   157	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   158	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   159	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   160	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   161	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   162	
   163	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   171	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   172	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   173	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   174	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   175	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   176	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   177	
   178	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   179	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   180	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   181	  sorry
   182	
   183	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   184	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   185	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   186	  sorry
   187	
   188	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   189	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   190	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   191	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   192	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   193	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   194

   134	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   135	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   136	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper

   140	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)

   190	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint

   192	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   194	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P

   196	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   197	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper

   200	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   202	  Distribution.map
   203	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   204	    (fun s =>
   205	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   206	
   207	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   208	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   209	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   210	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   212	-/
   213	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   214	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   215	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  deriving DecidableEq
   218	
   219	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   220	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   300	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   301	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   302	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   303	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   304	
   305	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   306	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   307	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   311	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   312	  open Classical in
   313	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   314	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   315	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   316	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   317	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   318	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   319	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   320	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   321	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   322	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   323	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   324	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   325	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   326	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   328	      else false
   329	
   330	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   331	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   332	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   333	-/
   334	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   335	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   336	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   337	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   338	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   339	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   340	  μ_prob := by sorry
   341	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   342	
   343	end

    58	/-- The observable associated with a binary measurement; formalization-only notation
    59	used in `thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:251-261`, paper

    61	def obsOf {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    62	    (M : Measurement (ZMod 2) ι) : Op ι :=
    63	  M.effect 0 - M.effect 1
    64	
    65	/-- The ideal two-qubit projector for one Magic Square output bit. The other
    66	qubit is marginalized by summing the two-qubit Pauli basis projectors. -/
    67	noncomputable def idealMagicBitProj (W : PauliKind) (b : ZMod 2) :
    68	    Op (Fin 2 → ZMod 2) :=
    69	  ∑ e : Fin 2 → ZMod 2, if e 0 = b then pauliProj W e else 0
    70	
    71	/-- The ideal state in `thm:ms-rigidity`: two EPR pairs followed by the
    72	auxiliary bipartite state, in local-player register order. -/
    73	noncomputable def idealMsState {ιA'' ιB'' : Type*}
    74	    [Fintype ιA''] [DecidableEq ιA''] [Fintype ιB''] [DecidableEq ιB'']
    75	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')) :
    76	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    77	      (((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'') × ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')) :=
    78	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (Fin 2 → ZMod 2)) aux)

    80	/-- The isometries and auxiliary unit state in the conclusion of
    81	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    82	structure MsRigidityWitness (S : Strategy msGame) where
    83	  ιA'' : Type
    84	  ιB'' : Type
    85	  [ιA''Fintype : Fintype ιA'']
    86	  [ιB''Fintype : Fintype ιB'']
    87	  [ιA''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA'']
    88	  [ιB''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB'']
    89	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'')
    91	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    92	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')
    93	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')
    94	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    95	
    96	attribute [instance] MsRigidityWitness.ιA''Fintype
    97	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''Fintype MsRigidityWitness.ιA''DecidableEq
    98	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''DecidableEq
    99	
   100	/-- Alice's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   101	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
   102	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   103	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   104	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
   105	      (conjIsometry w.φA
   106	        (((S.A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
   107	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
   108	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιA'')) 1)
   109	    (idealMsState w.aux)
   110	
   111	/-- Bob's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   112	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
   113	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   114	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   115	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
   116	      (conjIsometry w.φB
   117	        (((S.B (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)))
   118	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
   119	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιB'')))
   120	    (idealMsState w.aux)
   121	
   122	/-- Alice's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
   123	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   124	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
   125	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
   126	  let X := heteroKron
   127	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
   128	  let Z := heteroKron
   129	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
   130	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   131	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
   132	
   133	/-- Bob's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
   134	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   135	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
   136	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
   137	  let X := heteroKron 1
   138	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   139	  let Z := heteroKron 1
   140	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   141	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   142	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
   143	
   144	/-- `thm:ms-rigidity`, imported from Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
   145	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
   147	
   148	The paper states the Euclidean estimate at scale `sqrt ε` at lines 624--626
   149	and explains the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650--652. One
   150	universal constant applies to every strategy and nonnegative error parameter. -/
   151	theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
   152	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   153	      ∀ S : Strategy msGame, 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   154	        ∃ w : MsRigidityWitness S,
   155	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealMsState w.aux‖ ≤
   156	              C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   157	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   158	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   159	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   160	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   161	          msAnticommutatorDistanceA S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   162	          msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   163	  sorry
   164	
   165	/-- The state of the perfect strategy constructed in `thm:ms-from-ac`. -/
   166	noncomputable def msPerfectState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   167	    [Nonempty ι] : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ι × ZMod 2) × (ι × ZMod 2)) :=
   168	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState ι) (eprState (ZMod 2)))
   169	
   170	/-- `thm:ms-from-ac`: any anticommuting pair of projective binary
   171	measurements, consistent on an EPR state, extends to a value-one SPCC Magic
   172	Square strategy. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:251-261`, paper
   173	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:654-722`.
   174	
   175	The local index type is arbitrary, finite, and nonempty; no field model or QPBT
   176	parameter is assumed. The equality `hι` identifies the target local Hilbert
   177	space with the constructed tensor factor. -/
   178	theorem exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting
   179	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   180	    (A B : Measurement (ZMod 2) ι)
   181	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   182	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B)
   183	    (hcA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn A (eprState ι))
   184	    (hcB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn B (eprState ι))
   185	    (hac : obsOf A * obsOf B = -(obsOf B * obsOf A)) :
   186	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy msGameSymm, ∃ hι : S.ι = (ι × ZMod 2),
   187	      S.IsSPCC ∧ S.toStrategy.value = 1 ∧
   188	      reindexState (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hι) (Equiv.cast hι)) S.ψ =
   189	        msPerfectState ι ∧
   190	      ∀ b : ZMod 2,
   191	        reindexOp (Equiv.cast hι.symm) ((S.M (.var 0)).effect (.bit b)) =
   192	            heteroKron (A.effect b) (1 : Op (ZMod 2)) ∧
   193	          reindexOp (Equiv.cast hι.symm) ((S.M (.var 4)).effect (.bit b)) =
   194	            heteroKron (B.effect b) (1 : Op (ZMod 2)) := by
   195	  sorry

   197	end

90	
    91	/-- Bounded multivariate polynomials form a finite set over a finite coefficient
    92	semiring. This is the finite outcome set required by `def:ld-meas`,
    93	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
    94	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
    95	noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m : ℕ) (K : Type*)
    96	    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by
    97	  letI : Finite ↥(polyFunc m K d) := Module.finite_of_finite K
    98	  exact Fintype.ofFinite _
    99	
   100	/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
   101	coefficient semiring. -/
   102	noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   103	    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
   104	
   105	/-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
   106	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   107	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   108	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
   109	
   110	/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
   111	have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
   112	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
   113	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   114	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   115	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   116	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   117	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   118	  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
   119	
   120	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   121	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   122	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   123	
   124	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   125	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   126	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   127	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   128	
   129	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   130	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   131	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   132	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   133	
   134	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   135	point question. -/
   136	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   137	  fun i => match i with
   138	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   139	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   140	  | .inr _ => 0
   141	
   142	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   143	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   144	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   145	
   146	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   147	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   148	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   149	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   150	  | .pointVals values => values
   151	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   152	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   153	
   154	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   155	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   156	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   157	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   158	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   159	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   160	
   161	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   162	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   163	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   164	
   165	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
   166	strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
   167	form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
   168	
   169	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   170	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   171	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   172	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   173	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   174	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   175	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   176	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   177	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   178	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   179	                (fun u outcome =>
   180	                  heteroKron
   181	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   182	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   183	                (fun u outcome =>
   184	                  heteroKron 1
   185	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   186	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   187	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   188	                (fun u outcome =>
   189	                  heteroKron
   190	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   191	                (fun u outcome =>
   192	                  heteroKron 1
   193	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   194	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
   195	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   196	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   197	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   198	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   199	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   200	  sorry
   201	
   202	end

   204	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
     8	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
     9	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, from
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
    16	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:430-454`,
    17	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
    32	
    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    47	
    48	/-- The local isometries, auxiliary spaces, and unit auxiliary state in
    49	`cor:pauli-binary`; this structure introduces no hypothesis beyond the paper
    50	theorem. -/
    51	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    52	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    53	  ιA' : Type
    54	  ιB' : Type
    55	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    56	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    57	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    58	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    59	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    60	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    61	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    63	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    64	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    65	
    66	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    68	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    69	
    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    72	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    73	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    74	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    75	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    76	  fun p q =>
    77	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    78	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
    79	    else 0
    80	
    81	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    82	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    83	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    84	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    85	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    86	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    87	  fun p q =>
    88	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    89	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.2.2 q.2.2
    90	    else 0
    91	
    92	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    93	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    94	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    95	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    96	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    97	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
    98	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    99	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   100	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   101	
   102	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   103	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   104	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   105	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   106	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   107	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   108	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   109	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   110	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   111	
   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   115	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   116	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   118	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   119	          (((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   120	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   121	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   122	
   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   125	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   126	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function
   470	of the parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$.
   471	The lemma also establishes the time complexity of computing the {description} of
   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.

   477	\begin{lemma}[Complexity of the classical low-degree test]

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}

   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.

   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,

   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test.    414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}

   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for

   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}

mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.

The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or

avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.

If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
the issue or pull request in a footnote.

\section{When the Investigation Starts}

The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
argument.

The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
relevant files already compile.

At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
formalized.

A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
mathematics.

Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
implementation.

\section{When to Write a Note}

A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
relation.

A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.

Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.

When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
though it were the paper theorem.

This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
argument.

A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.

\section{Counterexamples}

If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.

\section{Revision of a Note}

A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
which point remains unsettled.

Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
discussion.

\section{Form of the Note}

Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
around the mathematical assertion and its proof.

The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.

Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.

Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
equations.

Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.

The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
footnotes.

The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,

    51	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    52	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    53	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    54	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    56	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    57	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    58	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    59	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    61	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    62	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    63	\end{enumerate}
    64	
    65	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    66	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    67	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    68	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    69	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    70	third form.
    71	
    72	\section{The source assertion}
    73	
    74	A two-player one-round game
    75	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    76	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    77	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    78	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    79	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    80	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    81	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    82	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    83	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    84	and the value of the game is the supremum
    85	\begin{equation*}
    86	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    87	\end{equation*}
    88	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    89	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    90	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    91	same measurements.
    92	
    93	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    94	\footnote{The statement is at
    95	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    96	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement restored to this form
    97	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
    98	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
    99	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   100	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   101	\begin{equation*}
   102	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   103	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   104	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   105	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   106	\end{equation*}
   107	
   108	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   109	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   110	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   111	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   112	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   113	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   114	\begin{equation*}
   115	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   116	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   117	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   118	\end{equation*}
   119	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   120	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   121	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   122	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   123	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   124	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   125	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   126	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   127	
   128	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   129	
   130	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   131	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   132	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   133	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   134	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   135	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   136	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   137	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   138	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   139	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   140	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   141	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   142	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   143	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   144	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   145	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   146	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   147	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   148	form.
   149	
   150	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   151	
   152	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   153	
   154	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   155	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   156	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   157	generality that it is projective.%
   158	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   159	lines~317--321.}
   160	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   161	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   162	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   163	
   164	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   165	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   166	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   167	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   168	lines~2322--2332.}
   169	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   170	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   171	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   172	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   173	not used.
   174	
   175	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   176	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   177	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   178	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint currently records the lemma as part of
   179	the games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on it; the two source
   180	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   181	development.  Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here
   182	--- requires the attainment form.
   183	
   184	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   185	
   186	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape.
   187	Its proof records the value-preserving construction and the approximate form
   188	that the construction yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment
   189	step as unproved, citing this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the
   190	obstruction.  An earlier revision of the blueprint had instead weakened the
   191	source-labelled conclusion to the approximate form; following the project's
   192	proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled statement is restored and the missing
   193	step is tracked in the proof rather than absorbed into the statement. The
   194	source-shaped declaration \leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is
   195	now linked to the lemma; its proof remains the tracked attainment obligation.
   196	
   197	\section{Conclusion}
   198	
   199	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   200	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   201	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   202	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built on
   203	the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   204	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   205	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   206	suffices.  For stage~4 (formalization) the recommendation is: formalize the
   207	given-strategy symmetrization lemma as the workhorse statement; keep the
   208	source-labelled lemma in source shape with the attainment step an explicit,
   209	tracked proof obligation; and do not strengthen the source-labelled statement's
   210	hypotheses or weaken its conclusion silently.  If a later investigation
   211	settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the statement should
   212	then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented statement
   213	correction.
   214	
   215	\bibliographystyle{alpha}
   216	\bibliography{references}
   217	
   218	\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\input{command}
+
+\title{Prime-Characteristic and Binary Pauli Observables}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-02}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+\section{At a glance}
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source-facing statements must retain
+  arbitrary prime characteristic while the later Pauli basis test uses a
+  separately named characteristic-two specialization.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The remaining proofs should occupy one
+  algebra file of roughly 100--200 lines.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Mathlib supplies finite matrix algebra
+  and finite-field facts; the generalized Pauli definitions and their
+  characteristic-two specialization are project-local.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Unitarity of shift and phase
+  matrices, the $p$-th-power identity, and additive-character orthogonality.
+  The scope correction is tracked in
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}
+  and descends from \localissue{0002}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb F_p$, let
+$\chi(x)=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_p}(x)/p)$, and let
+$a,a',b\in K^n$.  The relevant identities are
+\[
+ \tau^W(a)\tau^W(a')=\tau^W(a+a'),\qquad
+ \tau^W(a)^p=I,
+\]
+and
+\[
+ \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)=\chi(-a\mathbin{\cdot}b)
+ \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
+\]
+The explicit shift and phase matrices are unitary. The second identity implies
+that every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $\tau^W(a)$ satisfies $\lambda^p=1$. If
+$V\leq K^n$ and $v\notin V^\perp$, Fourier cancellation takes the form
+\[
+ \mathbb E_{u\in V}\chi(u\mathbin{\cdot}v)=0.
+\]
+
+\section{Source and formal scope}
+The source defines the shift and phase matrices and states their product,
+$p$-th-power, unitarity, spectral, and twisted-commutation properties in
+\cite[lines 1056--1095]{Ji2020MIPStar}. It uses the same character for Fourier
+cancellation over a subspace at lines 1124--1132 and extends the twisted
+relation to several qudits at lines 1141--1150. These assertions depend on the
+characteristic $p$; they are not intrinsically binary.
+
+The formal definitions \path{primeTauShift}, \path{primeTauPhase}, and
+\path{primeTauObservable} use the canonical character \path{ffChar} in
+characteristic $p$.  Their theorem statements cover the identities above for
+arbitrary $p$.  The declarations whose names begin with
+\path{tauObservable} or use \path{phaseSign} instead specialize to
+$p=2$, where $\chi(x)=(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(x)}$.  This specialization is
+appropriate only for the subsequent test, whose admissible sizes satisfy
+$q=2^k$; it is not substituted for the general statements.
+
+The proofs can be obtained directly from the displayed matrices.  A shift is a
+permutation matrix, a phase matrix has diagonal entries of modulus one, and a
+tensor product of such matrices is unitary.  Iterating the product identity
+gives $\tau^W(a)^p=I$.  Applying this equality to a nonzero eigenvector gives
+$(\lambda^p-1)v=0$, hence $\lambda^p=1$.  Finally, when
+$v\notin V^\perp$, the map $u\mapsto\chi(u\cdot v)$ is a nontrivial character
+of the finite additive group $V$, so its average vanishes.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization}
+The source-general definitions and results are linked from
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex}, lines~553--633 and
+649--660. Their Lean declarations are \leanid{primeTauShift},
+\leanid{primeTauPhase}, \leanid{primeTauObservable}, and the accompanying
+product, power, unitarity, spectral, commutation, and cancellation theorems.
+They quantify an arbitrary prime characteristic and use the corresponding
+additive character.
+
+The separately named binary declarations are used by the later QPBT chapters.
+They specialize the same formulas to characteristic two and are not linked as
+implementations of the unrestricted source nodes. Thus the blueprint, the
+general Lean interface, and the paper agree; the binary layer is a consumer
+specialization rather than a restriction of the source statement.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+There is no mathematical restriction in the source-facing formal statements:
+they retain arbitrary prime characteristic and the corresponding canonical
+character.  The characteristic-two declarations are separate corollaries for
+the QPBT parameter regime.  The remaining work is to prove the general
+identities from the explicit matrices and character orthogonality; it does not
+require changing the binary operator definitions.
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+
+\title{The Exponent Comparison in the Canonical Pauli Basis Test Bound}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-02}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  One intermediate inequality in the source
+  does not follow from the canonical parameter definition, but the claimed
+  soundness bound follows by estimating the same term directly.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The remaining formal argument is an
+  elementary real-analytic estimate of roughly 30--60 lines.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Mathlib supplies inequalities for real
+  powers, exponentials, and logarithms; the project-specific step unfolds the
+  canonical parameters and soundness function.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The function
+  $(\log R)^{a+b}R^{-b}$ is bounded for $R\geq 4$, and the canonical lower and
+  upper bounds on $m$ transfer this estimate to the third soundness term.
+  Tracked in
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16};
+  the parent blueprint task is \localissue{0002}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $a\geq 1$ and $0<b<1$ be the universal constants, and let $\eps\geq0$ be a
+failure-probability parameter.  The soundness function is
+\[
+  \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)
+    = a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd}\bigr).
+\]
+For $R\geq4$, let $c$ be the least even integer at least $(a+b)/b$, set
+$k=c\lceil\log_2\log_2 R\rceil+1$ and $q=2^k$, and let $j$ be determined by
+$2^j\leq c\lceil\log_2 R\rceil+1<2^{j+1}$. The remaining canonical parameters
+are $m=2^j$ and $d=1$. In particular,
+$m\geq (c/2)\log_2 R\geq\log_2 R$. The required estimate for the third summand is
+\[
+  a m^a 2^{-bm} \leq C'(\log R)^{-b},
+\]
+for a constant $C'$ depending only on $a$ and $b$.  This estimate, together
+with the source bounds for the first two summands, gives the asserted
+polylogarithmic bound for $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$.
+
+\section{The source comparison}
+
+The canonical parameters are defined in \cite[lines~1503--1514]{Ji2020MIPStar},
+and the bound and its proof occupy lines~1520--1562. At line~1543 the proof
+replaces $2^{-bmd}$ by $q^{-b}$ using the assertion $k\leq m$.%
+\footnote{Tracked in
+\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}.
+The canonical parameter definition is at
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
+lines~1503--1514; the bound and its proof are at lines~1520--1562, with the
+disputed comparison at line~1543.}
+That comparison does not follow from the stated parameter choice.  For example,
+the allowed values $a=1$ and $b=1/2$ give $c=4$, and $R=5$ gives $k=9$ but
+$m=8$.  Thus the displayed justification is false even though the lemma's
+conclusion remains valid.
+
+The third term can instead be bounded independently of $q$.  Since $d=1$ and
+$m\geq (c/2)\log R\geq\log R$,
+\[
+  2^{-bm}\leq R^{-b}.
+\]
+The accompanying upper bound $m\leq 2c\log R$ therefore gives
+\[
+  a m^a2^{-bm}
+    \leq a(2c)^a(\log R)^aR^{-b}
+    = a(2c)^a\bigl((\log R)^{a+b}R^{-b}\bigr)(\log R)^{-b}.
+\]
+The parenthesized factor is bounded on $R\geq4$: it is continuous and tends
+to zero as $R$ tends to infinity.  Absorbing its supremum into the universal
+constant yields the required estimate.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+
+The blueprint makes explicit the nonnegative failure-probability domain
+implicit in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} and otherwise retains the source statement.
+The formal theorem records the same faithful boundary hypothesis and
+conclusion; its docstring marks the corrected intermediate argument and cites
+this note.%
+\footnote{The formal statement is
+\leanid{exists\_deltaQld\_introParams\_bound} in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/CanonicalParams.lean}.}
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The source's comparison $k\leq m$ is false for some permitted constants and
+values of $R$.  It is not needed: for nonnegative failure parameters, the
+canonical lower bound on $m$ controls the third soundness term directly and
+proves the same final estimate after enlarging the universal constant.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\input{command}
+
+\title{Index Pairing in the Low-Degree Sandwich}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low. The source has a typographical mismatch
+  between a measurement family and the outcome supplied to it.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction changes only the displayed
+  index pairing; the imported proof applies without a new estimate.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} No Mathlib result is needed to identify
+  the mismatch. The formal statement uses a dependent family of outcome types.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Each projector must receive an
+  outcome from its own alphabet, and an empty ordered product equals the
+  identity. The correction is tracked in
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}
+  and descends from \localissue{0002}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms: the printed statement}
+For $i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, let $G^{i,x}$ be a projective measurement with
+outcome set $\mathcal G_i$. The source prints the sandwich as
+\[
+  G^{k,x}_{g_1}\cdots G^{1,x}_{g_k}\cdots G^{k,x}_{g_1}.
+\]
+This expression is not defined for a general family of outcome sets: the
+outer factor belongs to the measurement indexed by $\mathcal G_k$, whereas
+$g_1$ belongs to $\mathcal G_1$. The mismatch occurs in
+\cite[lines~465--501, especially lines~484--488]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
+
+The result is imported there from Fact~4.34 of the NEEXP paper
+\cite[lines~952--973, especially lines~965--968]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, mirrored
+at \path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex}. That statement
+pairs every measurement with its own outcome, giving
+\[
+  G^{k,x}_{g_k}\cdots G^{2,x}_{g_2}G^{1,x}_{g_1}
+  G^{2,x}_{g_2}\cdots G^{k,x}_{g_k}.
+\]
+The order of the operators is unchanged; only the subscripts are corrected.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization}
+The blueprint uses the type-correct pairing in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, lines~398--425, and explains
+the discrepancy at lines~430--432 in \path{rem:ld-sandwich-indexing}. The formal definition
+\leanid{sandwichProduct} uses an outcome function whose value at $i$ belongs
+to the outcome type of $G^i$. Thus every operator receives the corresponding
+component $g_i$. When $k=0$, the product is empty and its value is the identity,
+which supplies the unique empty-tuple outcome.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+The reversed outcome subscripts in the source are a typographical error, not a
+different mathematical construction. The blueprint and Lean statement retain
+the source's operator order while restoring the only type-correct pairing.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+
+\title{Polynomial Error Notation and Square-Root Bounds}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The paper's global polynomial shorthand
+  couples two constants in a way that excludes a square-root function used
+  explicitly later in the same paper.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The formal correction is one predicate with
+  separate prefactor and exponent witnesses; no theorem statement changes.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The obstruction is elementary real
+  analysis.  Mathlib's real-power API will discharge concrete downstream
+  witnesses, while the corrected convention is project-local.
+  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs.} The downstream witnesses use the
+  \path{Real.rpow} API.  The obstruction here is the elementary fact that no
+  constant $C>0$ can bound $\sqrt{x}$ by $C x^C$ for every $x>0$.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+The paper's shorthand asks for one universal constant $C>0$ such that
+\[
+  f(x) \leq Cx^C \qquad (x>0).
+\]
+The formal one-parameter convention instead asks for constants $A\geq1$ and
+$r>0$ such that
+\[
+  0\leq f(x)\leq Ax^r \qquad (x\geq0).
+\]
+This form includes $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ by taking $A=1$ and $r=1/2$.
+
+\section{The source convention}
+
+The asymptotic conventions of \cite[lines~23--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} define
+$f(x)=\operatorname{poly}(x)$ using the same constant as prefactor and
+exponent.  Later, the Pauli basis analysis explicitly obtains
+$\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ and
+$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt{\eps}$ at lines~508--520 and 649--676 of
+the chapter-14 source mirror.\footnote{The corresponding files are
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex} and
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.  The
+formal correction is tracked in
+\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/16}{GitHub issue \#16}
+and descends from \localissue{0002}.}
+
+The coupled-constant inequality cannot hold for $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$.  At $x=1$ it
+would imply $C\geq1$.  For such a constant,
+\[
+  \frac{\sqrt{x}}{Cx^C}=C^{-1}x^{1/2-C}
+\]
+is unbounded as $x$ decreases to zero, contradicting the proposed inequality
+on all positive inputs.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+
+The blueprint records only the paper's local assertions that the relevant
+errors are polynomial in $\eps$; those assertions include the displayed
+square-root choices.  The formal helper therefore separates the prefactor and
+exponent.\footnote{The helper is \leanid{IsPolyErr} in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean}.}  This changes no
+source-labelled theorem and preserves the intended meaning that the error
+decays as a positive power of its argument.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The single-constant shorthand is incompatible with the paper's own
+square-root error functions.  Using independent positive exponent and
+prefactor witnesses is a local correction to that shorthand, not an
+unfaithful theorem dependency.
+

    74	section Fourier
    75	
    76	-- The Fourier section uses `[Fintype F]` (rather than `[Finite F]` as in the Trace section)
    77	-- because `AddChar.expect_eq_ite` requires a `Fintype` instance. Downstream users with
    78	-- only `[Finite F]` can obtain `Fintype` via `Fintype.ofFinite`.
    79	variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    80	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
    81	
    82	/-- The canonical complex additive character `x ↦ ω^{tr[x]}` on `F`. -/
    83	noncomputable abbrev ffChar : AddChar F ℂ :=
    84	  (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p)).compAddMonoidHom (Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F).toAddMonoidHom
    85	
    86	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    87	@[simp] theorem ffChar_apply (x : F) :
    88	    ffChar (p := p) (F := F) x =
    89	      ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p) (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) :=
    90	  rfl
    91	
    92	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    93	private theorem ffTrace_nondegenerate [Finite F] (a : F) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    94	    ∃ b : F, ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (a * b) ≠ 0 := by
    95	  haveI : CharP F p := (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod p) F p).mp (ZMod.charP p)
    96	  have hp : p = ringChar F := by
    97	    simpa using (ringChar.eq F p).symm
    98	  subst p
    99	  simpa [ffTrace] using (FiniteField.trace_to_zmod_nondegenerate F (a := a) ha)
   100	
   101	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   102	private theorem ffChar_ne_zero [Finite F] : ffChar (p := p) (F := F) ≠ 0 := by
   103	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   104	  obtain ⟨a, ha0⟩ :=
   105	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := (1 : F)) one_ne_zero
   106	  have ha : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) a ≠ 0 := by
   107	    simpa using ha0
   108	  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
   109	  rw [ffChar_apply]
   110	  intro h
   111	  exact ha ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   112	
   113	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-scalar`.
   114	
   115	The Fourier orthogonality relation for the finite field `F`: the expectation
   116	of the additive character `ω^{tr[x·a]}` over `x ∈ F` equals `1` when `a = 0`
   117	and `0` otherwise. -/
   118	theorem fourier_fact_scalar (a : F) :
   119	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) =
   120	      if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   121	  let ψ : AddChar F ℂ := (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).mulShift a
   122	  calc
   123	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) = 𝔼 x : F, ψ x := by
   124	      simp [ψ, AddChar.mulShift_apply, mul_comm]
   125	    _ = if ψ = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := AddChar.expect_eq_ite ψ
   126	    _ = if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   127	      by_cases ha : a = 0
   128	      · have hψ : ψ = 0 := by
   129	          ext x
   130	          simp [ψ, ha]
   131	        simp [ha, hψ]
   132	      · have hψ : ψ ≠ 0 := by
   133	          have hprimitive : (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).IsPrimitive := by
   134	            exact AddChar.IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (by
   135	              simpa [AddChar.one_eq_zero] using (ffChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F)))
   136	          simpa [ψ, AddChar.one_eq_zero] using hprimitive ha
   137	        simp [ha, hψ]

   139	section Vector
   140	
   141	variable {m : ℕ}
   142	
   143	-- We define `ffDotProduct` directly rather than reusing `Matrix.dotProduct` to avoid
   144	-- pulling in the full `Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic` import. The definitions are identical.
   145	/-- The standard dot product on `F^m`. -/
   146	def ffDotProduct (u v : Fin m → F) : F :=
   147	  ∑ i, u i * v i
   148	
   149	/-- The additive character `u ↦ ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` on `F^m`. -/
   150	noncomputable def ffVecChar (v : Fin m → F) : AddChar (Fin m → F) ℂ :=
   151	  (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).compAddMonoidHom
   152	    { toFun := fun u => ffDotProduct u v
   153	      map_zero' := by simp [ffDotProduct]
   154	      map_add' := by
   155	        intro u w
   156	        simp [ffDotProduct, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib] }
   157	
   158	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   159	@[simp] theorem ffVecChar_apply (u v : Fin m → F) :
   160	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   161	      ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (ffDotProduct u v) :=
   162	  rfl
   163	
   164	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   165	private theorem ffVecChar_ne_zero [Finite F] {v : Fin m → F} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   166	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 := by
   167	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   168	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
   169	    simpa [funext_iff] using hv
   170	  obtain ⟨b, hb0⟩ :=
   171	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := v i) hi
   172	  have hb : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (b * v i) ≠ 0 := by
   173	    simpa [mul_comm] using hb0
   174	  refine ⟨Pi.single i b, ?_⟩
   175	  have hdot : ffDotProduct (Pi.single i b) v = b * v i := by
   176	    unfold ffDotProduct
   177	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
   178	    · simp
   179	    · intro j _ hji
   180	      simp [hji]
   181	    · intro hi
   182	      exact (hi (by simp)).elim
   183	  rw [ffVecChar_apply, hdot, ffChar_apply]
   184	  intro h
   185	  exact hb ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   186	
   187	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-vector`.
   188	
   189	The vector version of Fourier orthogonality: the expectation of the additive
   190	character `ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` over `u ∈ F^m` equals `1` when `v = 0`
   191	and `0` otherwise. -/
   192	theorem fourier_fact_vector (v : Fin m → F) :
   193	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   194	      if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   195	  calc
   196	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   197	        if ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 :=
   198	      AddChar.expect_eq_ite _
   199	    _ = if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   200	      by_cases hv : v = 0
   201	      · have hzero :
   202	            ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 := by
   203	          subst v
   204	          ext u
   205	          simp [ffVecChar, ffDotProduct]
   206	        rw [if_pos hzero, if_pos hv]
   207	      · have hvc : ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 :=
   208	          ffVecChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F) hv
   209	        simp [hv, hvc]
   210	
   211	end Vector
   212	end Fourier
